answer.rationale: The 18% spend cut mandate collides with a 14-day contract expiration and 94% line utilization. Switching vendors (memory_c2 shows cost reduction but demands onboarding risk we cannot absorb at 94% capacity). Renewing carries no migration friction (memory_c1) but forgoes the 18% target. Deferring is impossible with no auto-renew clause. Adding a second source requires duplicate qualification time we do not have. Negotiating builds directly on memory_c4's proven success—benchmarking recovered real margin at the last renewal. The incumbent has already demonstrated willingness to move on price and terms. A targeted negotiation positions us to hit the 18% target while preserving the integration stability we depend on at high utilization. Verifying memory_c4 confirms the specific benchmarking tactics and outcome ranges to anchor our negotiation floor. This preserves optionality: if the incumbent will not move sufficiently, we retain the option to escalate to a vendor switch or defer into Q2 when line utilization risk is lower. The primary risk is delivery disruption if negotiation fails and we have insufficient time to execute an alternative—flagged for mitigation planning.
